1. Yes, I would perform rifampicin drug-resistance testing on this patient's initial diagnostic specimen. This is because drug-resistant TB is a significant concern, especially in cases where the patient has no known drug-resistant contact but has a positive M. tuberculosis test. Resistance testing can help guide appropriate treatment and prevent the spread of drug-resistant TB.

2. I would send a mycobacterial culture on this patient once a sputum or gastric aspirate specimen is obtained. This is because culture is the gold standard for diagnosing TB and can provide information about the strain of TB, drug susceptibility patterns, and the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of the drugs, which can be crucial for determining the appropriate treatment regimen.
